page.layout: One printed page. Upper part: a chronological table with its column headings above, seven columns (Anni ante ord.Iul., Aureus num., Anni O-lymp., An.Vrb. coditae., Literae domin., Nabonassari, Feriae), one line per year. Lower part: one column of running text in full width, with a paragraph marked 4 at its start. No margin notes.

main_text.l: Anni ante ord.Iul. | Aureus num. | Anni O-lymp. | An.Vrb. coditae. | Literae domin. | Nabona-sari | Feriae
main_text.p: 4 Hoc anno Nabonasari 366, die 26 Thoth, in Babylone conspecta est eclipsis lunaris, sole occupante 28 gradum Sagittarii, ut ex traditione Hipparchi refert Ptolemaeus lib. 4 Almagesti, capite 11, Thoth Nabonasari 366 incurrit in 27 Nouembris, feriam quintam, labente anno 358 ante ordinationem Iulianam: itaque dies 26 Thoth incidit in 22 Decembris, feriam secundam, qua fuit eclipsis in oppositione luminarium. Hinc sequitur decimo quinto die ante, nimirum 8 Decembris fuisse nouilunium: quod etiam ostendit enneadecaeteris Iuliana. Aureus enim numerus anni 338 ante ordinationem Iulianam est v. qui in calendario Iuliano ponitur ad 17 kal. Maij, & recurrit die 7 Decembris: quia vero ab epocha Iuliani nouilunii elapsis annis 338 facta est anticipatio lunaris per diem unum, intelligi-tur no-

page.notes: Doubtful: the "18" before "I" in the row for 342 (printed "I8 — I"), read as 18 with [?] not added since the figure is clear enough but its place in the cell is unusual. The feriae "1" after "29 Nou." may be the Roman I. The marks "a366" and "b367" in the Nabonassari column are printed small letters, kept as they stand. Long s is rendered as s throughout (confpecta, eft, ostendit etc.), and u/v and i/j are normalised. The running head is printed in letter-spaced capitals. The paragraph continues on the next page after "no-".
